objects.description: Half-precision floating-point type. On ARM NEON, it aliases the native __fp16. Otherwise it's a small class wrapping a custom fp<1,5,10> representation with conversions to/from float. getBits/makeHalf provide raw 16-bit access. Literal operator _h constructs from a long double literal via float.

Templated 2D vector class holding two components of arithmetic type T. Provides array-style access, named swizzles (x/y, s/t, r/g), arithmetic, comparison, and common vector functions through inherited operator helper bases. Constructors support default, splat-from-scalar, per-component, and converting copy from another TVec2 with different component type. Also declares a friend constexpr 2D cross product (scalar) between two 2D vectors. This header also defines a family of aliases mapping common scalar types to concrete 2D vector typedefs (double2, float2, etc.). Details like helper base classes and macros (e.g., MATH_EMPTY_BASES, enable_if_arithmetic_t) are declared in included headers and not defined here.

Templated 3-component math vector with swizzles and arithmetic/comparison/operator mixins. Stores three values of type T and provides array-style access, named components (x/y/z, r/g/b, s/t/p), 2D sub-vectors, multiple constructors (scalar splat, component-wise, from TVec2 + scalar, and converting copy), and a friend cross() function. Inherits behavior from math operator/mixin bases declared elsewhere. Aliases provide common concrete instantiations (double3, float3, etc.). Construction/destruction are trivial; no ownership semantics. Unknown macros/classes (MATH_EMPTY_BASES, TVecProductOperators, TVecAddOperators, TVecUnaryOperators, TVecComparisonOperators, TVecFunctions, enable_if_arithmetic_t, arithmetic_result_t, TVec2) are referenced but defined in other headers.

Templated 4-component vector type providing arithmetic, comparison, and utility functions via mixin operator/function bases. Stores components in a union with multiple semantic aliases (x/y/z/w, r/g/b/a, s/t/p/q) and swizzle sub-vectors (TVec2, TVec3). Suitable for math operations on 4D vectors of arithmetic types. Construction supports scalars, per-component values, and combinations of TVec2/TVec3 with scalars. Full behavior of operator bases and TVec2/TVec3 depends on their definitions in other headers. Destruction is trivial; no ownership semantics.

Type alias for a single-precision quaternion. Canonical pointer type refers to the underlying templated quaternion instantiation.
Type alias for a half-precision quaternion. Canonical pointer type refers to the underlying templated quaternion instantiation.
Type alias for a 2x2 matrix of doubles in namespace filament::math. Behaves exactly like TMat22<double>.
Type alias for a 2x2 matrix of floats in namespace filament::math. Behaves exactly like TMat22<float>.

Template class representing a 3x3 column-major matrix with rich arithmetic, transform, and utility operations. Provides multiple constructors (identity, scalar, diagonal vector, columns, elements, quaternion, row-major tag), and static helpers like lookTo, getTransformForNormals, translation/scaling, and packing a tangent frame into a quaternion. Intended for math operations in Filament. Destruction is trivial; no dynamic ownership. Template parameter T is the scalar element type.

Type alias for a 4x4 matrix of floats (TMat44<float>). Provides all TMat44 functionality specialized for single precision.

template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T, typename U>
inline constexpr arithmetic_result_t<T, U> distance2(const VECTOR<T>& lv, const VECTOR<U>& rv)
functions.description: Returns the squared Euclidean distance: length2(rv - lv).
requirements: Same size vectors
VECTOR must implement operator[] and size()
T and U must support subtraction; length2 must be defined for the resulting vector type

functions.name: filament::math::details::normalize
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> normalize(const VECTOR<T>& lv)
functions.description: Returns a normalized (unit length) vector: lv / length(lv).
requirements: VECTOR must implement operator[] and size()
length(lv) must not be zero (no component is defined if the length is 0)
T must support division and construction from literal 1

functions.name: filament::math::details::rcp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> rcp(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Returns the element-wise reciprocal: 1 / v.
requirements: Each component of v must be non-zero to avoid division by zero
T must support division and construction from literal 1

functions.name: filament::math::details::abs
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> abs(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Returns the element-wise absolute value.
requirements: T must support comparison with 0 and unary negation
VECTOR must implement operator[] and size()

functions.name: filament::math::details::floor
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> floor(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies std::floor to each component of the vector.
requirements: T must be compatible with std::floor(T)

functions.name: filament::math::details::ceil
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> ceil(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies std::ceil to each component of the vector.
requirements: T must be compatible with std::ceil(T)

functions.name: filament::math::details::round
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> round(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies std::round to each component of the vector.
requirements: T must be compatible with std::round(T)

functions.name: filament::math::details::fmod
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T, typename U>
inline VECTOR<T> fmod(const VECTOR<T>& x, const VECTOR<U>& y)
functions.description: Element-wise floating-point remainder with truncation toward zero: std::fmod(x[i], y[i]).
requirements: x and y must have the same size()
Each y[i] must be non-zero
T and U must be compatible with std::fmod

functions.name: filament::math::details::remainder
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T, typename U>
inline VECTOR<T> remainder(const VECTOR<T>& x, const VECTOR<U>& y)
functions.description: Element-wise floating-point remainder as defined by std::remainder.
requirements: x and y must have the same size()
Each y[i] must be non-zero
T and U must be compatible with std::remainder

functions.name: filament::math::details::remquo
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T, typename U>
inline VECTOR<T> remquo(const VECTOR<T>& x, const VECTOR<U>& y, VECTOR<int>* q)
functions.description: Element-wise remquo operation; returns remainders and stores low-order bits of the quotients into q[i] via std::remquo.
requirements: x and y must have the same size()
q must be non-null and point to a VECTOR<int> of the same size()
Each y[i] must be non-zero
T and U must be compatible with std::remquo

functions.name: filament::math::details::inversesqrt
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> inversesqrt(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies 1/std::sqrt to each component (element-wise inverse square root).
requirements: Each v[i] should be > 0 for real-valued results
T must be compatible with std::sqrt and division

functions.name: filament::math::details::sqrt
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> sqrt(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies std::sqrt to each component (element-wise square root).
requirements: Each v[i] should be >= 0 for real-valued results
T must be compatible with std::sqrt

functions.name: filament::math::details::cbrt
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> cbrt(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies std::cbrt to each component (element-wise cubic root).
requirements: T must be compatible with std::cbrt

functions.name: filament::math::details::exp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> exp(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies std::exp to each component (element-wise exponential).
requirements: T must be compatible with std::exp

functions.name: filament::math::details::sign
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> sign(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Returns the sign of each component using std::copysign(1, v[i]) (components become -1 or +1, preserving sign).
requirements: T must be compatible with std::copysign and constructible from 1

functions.name: filament::math::details::pow
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> pow(VECTOR<T> v, T p)
functions.description: Raises each component of v to the scalar power p: std::pow(v[i], p).
requirements: T must be compatible with std::pow
Domain restrictions follow std::pow (e.g., negative bases with non-integer exponents may be NaN)

functions.name: filament::math::details::log
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> log(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies natural logarithm to each component: std::log(v[i]).
requirements: Each v[i] must be > 0 for real-valued results
T must be compatible with std::log

functions.name: filament::math::details::log10
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> log10(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies base-10 logarithm to each component: std::log10(v[i]).
requirements: Each v[i] must be > 0 for real-valued results
T must be compatible with std::log10

functions.name: filament::math::details::log2
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline VECTOR<T> log2(VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Applies base-2 logarithm to each component: std::log2(v[i]).
requirements: Each v[i] must be > 0 for real-valued results
T must be compatible with std::log2

functions.name: filament::math::details::saturate
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> saturate(const VECTOR<T>& lv)
functions.description: Clamps each component of lv to the [0, 1] range.
requirements: T must support comparison with 0 and 1 and be constructible from those literals

functions.name: filament::math::details::clamp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> clamp(VECTOR<T> v, T min, T max)
functions.description: Clamps each component of v to the closed interval [min, max] using scalar bounds.
requirements: T must support comparison and be constructible/copied
Assumes min <= max; undefined results if not

functions.name: filament::math::details::fma
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> fma(const VECTOR<T>& lv, const VECTOR<T>& rv, VECTOR<T> a
functions.description: Computes a += lv * rv element-wise and returns the result (a simple multiply-then-add; not a hardware fused operation).
requirements: All vectors must have the same size()
T must support operator* and operator+=

functions.name: filament::math::details::mix
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> mix(const VECTOR<T>& u, VECTOR<T> v, T a)
functions.description: Linear interpolation between vectors: u*(1-a) + v*a applied per component.
requirements: u and v must have the same size()
T must support arithmetic operations +, -, *
Typically a is in [0,1] for interpolation; extrapolation allowed but may be unintended

functions.name: filament::math::details::smoothstep
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> smoothstep(T edge0, T edge1, VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Hermite smoothstep; clamps t=(v-edge0)/(edge1-edge0) to [0,1] then returns t*t*(3-2*t) per component.
requirements: edge1 - edge0 must not be 0 to avoid division by zero
T must support arithmetic and comparison
v.size() is the vector dimension

functions.name: filament::math::details::step
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr VECTOR<T> step(T edge, VECTOR<T> v)
functions.description: Returns a per-component step: 0 if v[i] < edge, else 1.
requirements: T must support comparison and construction from 0 and 1

functions.name: filament::math::details::any
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr bool any(const VECTOR<T>& v)
functions.description: Returns true if any component is non-zero.
requirements: T must support comparison with 0

functions.name: filament::math::details::all
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class VECTOR, typename T>
inline constexpr bool all(const VECTOR<T>& v)
functions.description: Returns true if all components are non-zero.
requirements: T must support comparison with 0

functions.name: filament::math::details::operator*
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T, typename U>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<arithmetic_result_t<T, U>> operator*(const QUATERNION<T>& q, const QUATERNION<U>& r)
functions.description: Quaternion-quaternion product. Computes the Hamilton product of two quaternions q and r, possibly with different scalar types, returning a quaternion with the arithmetic_result_t<T,U> element type. Use to compose rotations or multiply general quaternions.
requirements: QUATERNION<T> exposes components x,y,z,w and a constructor compatible with QUATERNION<arithmetic_result_t<T,U>>(w,x,y,z).
No normalization is enforced; if representing rotations, callers typically provide unit quaternions to avoid scaling.
No side effects or error signaling; purely functional.

functions.name: filament::math::details::dot
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T, typename U>
inline constexpr arithmetic_result_t<T, U> dot(const QUATERNION<T>& p, const QUATERNION<U>& q)
functions.description: Dot product between two quaternions. Sums pairwise products of components (x,y,z,w). Useful for measuring similarity (e.g., in slerp) or computing norms.
requirements: Inputs may have different scalar types; result type is arithmetic_result_t<T,U>.
No additional constraints beyond valid quaternion components.

functions.name: filament::math::details::norm
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline T norm(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Euclidean norm (magnitude) of a quaternion, equivalent to sqrt(dot(q,q)). Alias of length().
requirements: Requires that sqrt is well-defined for dot(q,q) (i.e., dot(q,q) >= 0 for real T).
No error signaling; returns a non-negative T.

functions.name: filament::math::details::length
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline T length(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Alias for norm(q). Returns the Euclidean magnitude of quaternion q.
requirements: Same as norm(q).

functions.name: filament::math::details::length2
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr T length2(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Squared Euclidean length of quaternion q, computed as dot(q,q). Avoids the square root when only the squared norm is needed.
requirements: No special constraints; purely algebraic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::normalize
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline QUATERNION<T> normalize(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Returns a normalized (unit-length) quaternion. If q has zero length, returns the identity quaternion QUATERNION<T>(1).
requirements: No preconditions; zero-length input is handled by returning identity.
Result is unit-length when q is non-zero.

functions.name: filament::math::details::conj
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<T> conj(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Returns the quaternion conjugate: (w, -x, -y, -z). Useful for inversion and negating the imaginary part.
requirements: No special constraints; purely algebraic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::inverse
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<T> inverse(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Returns the multiplicative inverse of quaternion q, computed as conj(q) / dot(q,q).
requirements: dot(q,q) must be non-zero (i.e., q must be invertible/non-zero) to avoid division by zero.
Behavior is undefined for the zero quaternion.

functions.name: filament::math::details::real
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr T real(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Extracts the real (scalar) component of quaternion q: w.
requirements: No special constraints.

functions.name: filament::math::details::imaginary
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr TVec3<T> imaginary(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Extracts the imaginary (vector) component of quaternion q as a TVec3<T>: (x,y,z).
requirements: QUATERNION<T> must expose q.xyz convertible to TVec3<T>.

functions.name: filament::math::details::unreal
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<T> unreal(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Returns a quaternion with the same imaginary part as q and zero real part: (q.xyz, 0).
requirements: QUATERNION<T> constructor must accept (TVec3<T>, T).

functions.name: filament::math::details::cross
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T, typename U>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<arithmetic_result_t<T, U>> cross(const QUATERNION<T>& p, const QUATERNION<U>& q)
functions.description: Returns the quaternion cross-part unreal(p * q), i.e., the product with real part zeroed. Useful in some quaternion algebra contexts.
requirements: Relies on quaternion multiplication operator* and unreal().
Inputs may have different scalar types.

functions.name: filament::math::details::exp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline QUATERNION<T> exp(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Quaternion exponential. Computes e^q using e^{w}[(sin(||v||)/||v||) v, cos(||v||)] where q = (v, w).
requirements: norm(q.xyz) must be non-zero to avoid division by zero in (sin(n)/n).
Uses std::exp, sin, cos on T; T should be floating-point for meaningful results.

functions.name: filament::math::details::log
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline QUATERNION<T> log(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Quaternion natural logarithm. For q = (v, w), returns [(acos(w/||q||)/||v||) v, log(||q||)].
requirements: ||q|| = norm(q) must be non-zero (q ≠ 0) to avoid division by zero in w/||q|| and log(||q||).
norm(q.xyz) must be non-zero to avoid division by zero in the vector scaling.
Input should satisfy |w/||q||| <= 1 for acos; violations due to numeric error are not clamped here.

functions.name: filament::math::details::pow
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline QUATERNION<T> pow(const QUATERNION<T>& q, T a)
functions.description: Quaternion power q^a for scalar exponent a. Implemented via polar form using ||q|| and acos(w/||q||): ||q||^a [normalize(v) sin(aθ), cos(aθ)] with θ = acos(w/||q||).
requirements: norm(q) must be non-zero to compute w/||q|| and ||q||^a.
The imaginary part v must have non-zero norm because normalize(v) is used.
Input should satisfy |w/||q||| <= 1 for acos; no explicit clamping here.

functions.name: filament::math::details::slerp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline QUATERNION<T> slerp(const QUATERNION<T>& p, const QUATERNION<T>& q, T t)
functions.description: Spherical linear interpolation between quaternions p and q at parameter t. Handles near-aligned quaternions by falling back to normalized lerp and ensures shortest-path interpolation by flipping q when needed.
requirements: For the general path, both p and q should be non-zero to avoid division by zero when computing cos_a = |dot(p,q)| / (||p|| ||q||).
t is a scalar interpolation parameter; typical range is [0,1] but not enforced.
Returns a normalized quaternion.

functions.name: filament::math::details::lerp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<T> lerp(const QUATERNION<T>& p, const QUATERNION<T>& q, T t)
functions.description: Linear interpolation between quaternions p and q: (1 - t) * p + t * q. Does not normalize the result.
requirements: t is a scalar interpolation parameter; no constraints enforced.
For rotation usage, consider normalizing (use nlerp or normalize(lerp(...))).

functions.name: filament::math::details::nlerp
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<T> nlerp(const QUATERNION<T>& p, const QUATERNION<T>& q, T t)
functions.description: Normalized linear interpolation: normalize(lerp(p, q, t)). Cheaper than slerp, producing unit-length output but not constant angular velocity.
requirements: No special constraints; normalize handles zero-length by returning identity.

functions.name: filament::math::details::positive
functions.signature:
template <template <typename> class QUATERNION, typename T>
inline constexpr QUATERNION<T> positive(const QUATERNION<T>& q)
functions.description: Returns q if w >= 0, otherwise returns -q. Useful to enforce a consistent sign convention for unit quaternions representing the same rotation.
requirements: No special constraints; purely algebraic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::gaussJordanInverse
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::gaussJordanInverse(MATRIX src)
functions.description: Computes the inverse of a square MATRIX using Gauss–Jordan elimination with partial pivoting (column-major). Intended for generic N×N matrices when no closed-form inverse is provided.
requirements: MATRIX must be a square matrix type with: value_type, NUM_ROWS, NUM_COLS, operator[] returning columns addressable as m[col][row].
Input matrix must be invertible (non-singular); no singularity checks are performed.
The function uses column-major conventions; caller must provide a MATRIX that matches this layout.
Elements must support arithmetic operations (division, subtraction, etc.).

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::fastInverse2
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::fastInverse2(const MATRIX& x)
functions.description: Analytically computes the inverse of a 2×2 matrix (column-major) using the closed-form formula.
requirements: MATRIX must represent a 2×2 matrix with value_type and operator[] as column-major m[col][row].
The determinant (a*d - b*c) must be non-zero; function does not check for singularity.
Elements must support division.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::fastInverse3
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::fastInverse3(const MATRIX& x)
functions.description: Analytically computes the inverse of a 3×3 matrix (column-major) using cofactors and determinant.
requirements: MATRIX must represent a 3×3 matrix with value_type and column-major operator[] access.
The determinant must be non-zero; behavior is undefined for singular matrices.
Elements must support arithmetic and division.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::cofactor
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::cofactor(const MATRIX& m)
functions.description: Computes the full cofactor matrix of a square matrix of arbitrary order using recursive minors (column-major).
requirements: MATRIX must be square and provide value_type, NUM_COLS, operator[] for column-major access.
Elements must support arithmetic.
This is a generic (potentially expensive) implementation; prefer fastCofactor2/3 for 2×2/3×3.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::fastCofactor2
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::fastCofactor2(const MATRIX& m)
functions.description: Computes the cofactor matrix for a 2×2 matrix using the closed-form result (column-major).
requirements: MATRIX must be 2×2 with value_type and column-major access.
Elements must support arithmetic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::fastCofactor3
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::fastCofactor3(const MATRIX& m)
functions.description: Computes the cofactor matrix for a 3×3 matrix using the closed-form expressions (column-major).
requirements: MATRIX must be 3×3 with value_type and column-major access.
Elements must support arithmetic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::cof
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX, typename = std::enable_if_t<MATRIX::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX::NUM_COLS, int>>
inline constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::cof(const MATRIX& matrix)
functions.description: Dispatches to the appropriate cofactor computation based on matrix size: 2×2 (fast), 3×3 (fast), otherwise generic cofactor().
requirements: MATRIX must be square (NUM_ROWS == NUM_COLS).
MATRIX must support column-major access and value_type.
For sizes other than 2 or 3, the generic cofactor() may be computationally expensive.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::det
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX, typename = std::enable_if_t<MATRIX::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX::NUM_COLS, int>>
inline constexpr typename MATRIX::value_type MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::det(const MATRIX& matrix)
functions.description: Computes the determinant of a square matrix of arbitrary order via recursive expansion, with specialized fast paths for 2×2 and 3×3 in the helper.
requirements: MATRIX must be square and provide value_type, NUM_ROWS, NUM_COLS, and column-major operator[] access.
Elements must support arithmetic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::inverse
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX, typename = std::enable_if_t<MATRIX::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX::NUM_COLS, int>>
inline constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::inverse(const MATRIX& matrix)
functions.description: Computes the inverse of a square matrix, dispatching by size: 2×2 and 3×3 use closed-form fast inverses; larger sizes use Gauss–Jordan elimination.
requirements: MATRIX must be square (NUM_ROWS == NUM_COLS) with column-major access and value_type.
Input must be invertible; no runtime singularity checks are performed and behavior is undefined otherwise.
Elements must support division and arithmetic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::multiply
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX_R, typename MATRIX_A, typename MATRIX_B, typename = std::enable_if_t<(
    MATRIX_A::NUM_COLS == MATRIX_B::NUM_ROWS &&
    MATRIX_R::NUM_COLS == MATRIX_B::NUM_COLS &&
    MATRIX_R::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX_A::NUM_ROWS), int>>
constexpr MATRIX_R MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::multiply(MATRIX_A lhs, MATRIX_B rhs)
functions.description: Multiplies two matrices lhs and rhs in column-major form and returns the result MATRIX_R. Implemented by multiplying lhs with each column of rhs.
requirements: Dimension constraints must hold: A.cols == B.rows; R.cols == B.cols; R.rows == A.rows.
All types must provide operator[] column access and support vector-matrix multiplication lhs * rhs[col].
Elements must support arithmetic.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::transpose
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX, typename = std::enable_if_t<MATRIX::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX::NUM_COLS, int>>
inline constexpr MATRIX MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::transpose(MATRIX m)
functions.description: Returns the transpose of a square matrix (column-major), swapping rows and columns.
requirements: MATRIX must be square and provide column-major access via operator[].
Elements must support assignment/copy.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::trace
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX, typename = std::enable_if_t<MATRIX::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX::NUM_COLS, int>>
inline constexpr typename MATRIX::value_type MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::trace(MATRIX m)
functions.description: Computes the trace of a square matrix, i.e., the sum of its diagonal elements.
requirements: MATRIX must be square and provide value_type and column-major access.
Elements must support addition and default-initialization of value_type.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::diag
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX, typename = std::enable_if_t<MATRIX::NUM_ROWS == MATRIX::NUM_COLS, int>>
inline constexpr typename MATRIX::col_type MATH_PURE filament::math::details::matrix::diag(MATRIX m)
functions.description: Extracts the main diagonal of a square matrix into a column vector of type MATRIX::col_type.
requirements: MATRIX must be square and define col_type and column-major access.
col_type must be indexable and assignable element-wise.

functions.name: filament::math::details::matrix::extractQuat
functions.signature:
template <typename MATRIX>
TQuaternion<typename MATRIX::value_type> filament::math::details::matrix::extractQuat(const MATRIX& mat)
functions.description: Extracts a unit quaternion from the upper-left 3×3 rotation portion of a matrix using a numerically stable method (similar to Eigen/Imath).
requirements: mat must be at least 3×3 with column-major access to indices [0..2][0..2].
The 3×3 portion should represent a proper rotation matrix for meaningful results; function does not orthonormalize.
Requires sqrt and arithmetic support on value_type.

functions.name: filament::math::details::operator*
functions.signature:

import struct
import random
import math
from typing import List

# This generator targets stubs that read raw bytes and memcpy them into float arrays.
# The stubs expect up to 16 bytes (4 floats) for a 2x2 matrix, or up to 8 bytes (2 floats)
# for a scaling vector. We produce a buffer that is interesting when interpreted as
# IEEE-754 single-precision floats, covering edge cases and diverse values, while
# remaining valid inputs for both stubs.

# Helper to pack a list of Python floats into bytes (little-endian IEEE-754 float32)
def _pack_f32(vals: List[float]) -> bytes:
    return b"".join(struct.pack('<f', v) for v in vals)

# Interesting float32 patterns to exercise math code paths
INTERESTING_SCALARS = [
    0.0, -0.0,  # zeros
    1.0, -1.0,  # unit magnitudes
    0.5, 2.0,  # simple fractions
    1e-37, -1e-37,  # subnormal/very small range (may flush to 0)
    1e-5, -1e-5,
    1e5, -1e5,  # large magnitudes
    math.pi, -math.pi,  # trig-relevant
    math.inf, -math.inf,  # infinities
    float('nan'),  # NaN
]

# Additional crafted values for rotation/scaling matrices
ANGLE_SET = [0.0, math.pi/6, math.pi/4, math.pi/2, math.pi, -math.pi/2]
SCALE_SET = [0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 2.0, 10.0, -0.5]

# Prebuilt 2x2 matrices (column-major) expressed as 4 floats:
# - Identity, zero, rotation, scaling, shear-like, singular matrices
PRESET_MATS = []

# Identity
PRESET_MATS.append([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
# Zero (singular)
PRESET_MATS.append([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
# Common rotations
for ang in ANGLE_SET:
    c = math.cos(ang)
    s = math.sin(ang)
    # 2D rotation in column-major: [[c, s], [-s, c]]
    PRESET_MATS.append([c, s, -s, c])
# Scales
for sx in SCALE_SET:
    for sy in SCALE_SET:
        PRESET_MATS.append([sx, 0.0, 0.0, sy])
# Shear-like and near-singular
PRESET_MATS.append([1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0])
PRESET_MATS.append([1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0])
PRESET_MATS.append([1.0, 0.99999994, -0.99999994, 1.0])

# Prebuilt scaling vectors (2 floats)
PRESET_SCALES = []
for sx in SCALE_SET:
    for sy in SCALE_SET:
        PRESET_SCALES.append([sx, sy])
# Include some interesting magnitudes
PRESET_SCALES.extend([
    [1e-6, 1e6],
    [1e6, 1e-6],
    [0.0, 1.0],
    [1.0, 0.0],
])


def _choose_interesting_floats(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[float]:
    vals = []
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            vals.append(rng.choice(INTERESTING_SCALARS))
        elif choice == 1:
            # Random magnitude with sign, spanning wide exponent range
            sign = -1.0 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 1.0
            exp = rng.uniform(-30, 30)  # covers subnormals to large values
            vals.append(sign * (10.0 ** exp) if rng.random() < 0.2 else sign * rng.uniform(1e-6, 1e6))
        elif choice == 2:
            # Trig-relevant small multiples of pi
            k = rng.choice([-2.0, -1.0, -0.5, -1/3, -0.25, 0.0, 0.25, 1/3, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0])
            vals.append(k * math.pi)
        elif choice == 3:
            # Uniform in a moderate range
            vals.append(rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0))
        else:
            # Denormal-ish tiny
            vals.append(rng.choice([1e-38, -1e-38, 1e-45, -1e-45]))
    return vals


def _build_mode_matrix(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 50% chance use a preset 2x2 matrix; else compose one:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        m = rng.choice(PRESET_MATS)
        return _pack_f32(m)
    # Compose rotation * scale or random floats
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        ang = rng.choice(ANGLE_SET) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.uniform(-math.tau, math.tau)
        c = math.cos(ang)
        s = math.sin(ang)
        sx = rng.choice(SCALE_SET) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.uniform(-5.0, 5.0)
        sy = rng.choice(SCALE_SET) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.uniform(-5.0, 5.0)
        # Rotation then scaling (R * S), column-major: columns scaled by sx, sy respectively
        m00 = c * sx
        m01 = s * sx
        m10 = -s * sy
        m11 = c * sy
        return _pack_f32([m00, m01, m10, m11])
    else:
        # Raw interesting floats to fill 4 entries
        return _pack_f32(_choose_interesting_floats(rng, 4))


def _build_mode_scale(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 60% use preset scales; otherwise mixed interesting values
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s = rng.choice(PRESET_SCALES)
    else:
        s = _choose_interesting_floats(rng, 2)
    return _pack_f32(s)


def _assemble_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # The fuzzer will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR once per stub invocation.
    # We want a single buffer that works well for both stubs if reused across runs.
    # Strategy: randomly choose one of two primary layouts:
    # - Layout A (matrix-first): 16 bytes (4 floats) for TMat22 construction.
    # - Layout B (scale-first): 8 bytes (2 floats) for TMat22::scaling, optionally
    #   followed by 8 more bytes to still be useful for the first stub.
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.5:
        # Matrix-first, always 16 bytes
        return _build_mode_matrix(rng)
    else:
        # Scale-first, 50% return only 8 bytes, 50% append another 8 bytes
        buf = _build_mode_scale(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return buf
        else:
            # Append more interesting data so the first stub can still use 4 floats
            buf += _build_mode_scale(rng)
            return buf[:16]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a buffer up to 16 bytes, valid for memcpy into float arrays
    data = _assemble_buffer(rng)
    # Ensure size <= 4096 (guaranteed here) and non-empty
    if not data:
        # Fallback: identity matrix
        data = _pack_f32([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    return data[:4096]
